Anna: Hey team — quick design check. Finalizing copy & a11y for the 'Quiet Window' suppression control. Screenshot (mock): https://imgur.com/abc123. Current label in mock: 'Quiet window (snooze notifications)'. I'm worried 'snooze' is ambiguous for ops users. Thoughts?
Mike: I think 'snooze' reads product-y. For on-call/alerting, folks expect 'suppress' or 'silence'. Maybe 'Suppress notifications' is clearer.
Sophie: +1 to 'Suppress notifications'. Also we should make the start/end time clear: people expect timezone context. Right now mock shows "Starts in 15m" which could be confusing.
Lorenzo: UX nit — the toggle state is green when active but the tooltip says 'Quiet window on'. For screen readers, aria-live updates would be good. Suggested aria-label: `aria-label="Quiet window on: suppressing notifications until 3:30 PM PDT"`.
Anna: Good call. How about phrasing: 'Suppress notifications — until 3:30 PM PDT' vs 'Quiet window (suppress notifications until 3:30 PM PDT)'? Which is more scannable?
sam-bot: preview: Generated example notification stream with suppression rules applied. 3 messages suppressed.
Mike: Prefer the shorter leading verb: 'Suppress notifications — until 3:30 PM PDT'. It's actionable and discoverable in lists.
Sophie: Also think about the compact list view: we show a pill with label and an icon. Icon only isn't enough for color-blind users. Add text and a visually-hidden label for the icon.
Lorenzo: Accessibility suggestion for keyboard users: when the suppression pill is focused, pressing Enter should open an inline editor (small panel) rather than a modal. Inline editor preserves context. We should ensure the panel has role="dialog" and initial focus on the end time input.
Anna: Inline panel makes sense for quick edits. If we do inline, the panel heading should be 'Suppress notifications' not 'Quiet window'. Keep consistent copy across surfaces.
Mike: Copy tweak for the end-time selector dropdown: currently shows 'Until' with options '15m, 1h, 4h, Custom'. Change 'Until' to 'Ends' — shorter and consistent with other scheduling UIs.
Sophie: For the preview overlay, we should surface which channels are affected (email, slack, pager). Mock currently only lists 'Slack' which could mislead. Add a small matrix: channel -> suppressed? (checkmark).
Lorenzo: Edge case: scheduled rotations. If a team's on-call rota changes while suppression is active, who owns the suppression? Probably the creator. Show 'Created by' in the pill hover and in the inline editor.
Anna: UX question: Should we show an expiration timestamp in UTC as well as local? Ops folks sometimes paste UTC into runbooks. Maybe show both, smaller / muted: 'Ends 3:30 PM PDT · 10:30 PM UTC'.
Mike: Yes. Show local primary, UTC secondary. Keep the secondary visually muted and aria-readable.
Sophie: Microcopy for the confirmation: when removing suppression, current toast says 'Suppression removed'. Maybe better: 'Notifications will be delivered immediately'. Clear about effect.
Lorenzo: Implementation note: API returns suppression as `{enabled: true, ends_at: "2026-03-23T15:30:00-07:00", creator: "anna"}`. Frontend should compute both local/UTC strings.
Anna: For the keyboard a11y announcement when suppression starts/stops, suggested message: 'Notifications suppressed until 3:30 PM PDT'. Should be announced via polite aria-live.
Mike: UX QA checklist: keyboard focus order, screenreader label on pill, color contrast for icon, preview shows channel matrix, 'Ends' wording change, toast copy tweak. I'll draft a small PR checklist.
Sophie: Small copy nit for the new inline editor header: use sentence case 'Suppress notifications' (not title case).
Anna: Thanks — I'll update the mocks and push a Figma link. Anyone want to weigh in on default duration? 1h vs 4h.
Mike: Default to 1h for ad-hoc suppression, with 'Remember my choice' for advanced users (persist across incidents).
Lorenzo: Consider a modal fallback for mobile where inline panel space is limited.
Anna: Great — I'll iterate and post updated mock here. :thumbsup:
sam-bot: deploy-bot: design file updated — new frames uploaded to Figma. Link: https://figma.com/file/xyz456
Anna: Cool, next steps: I'll update copy strings, aria labels, and add the QA checklist to the PR description. Thanks all!
